name: Tempester n°18: a SysEx received over USB no longer clears the DIN running status
explanation: [routine] ([routine]) wrote [address] = 0 (DIN running status) unconditionally at four places: case 5C, case 60, cases 61/62 last chunk and case 70 last chunk. For a DIN SysEx the write is needed and harmless: it takes the DIN parser out of its F0 header mode (2e8 = 0xF0; otherwise the following data bytes are counted again as a SysEx header and [routine](F0) re-enters [routine]), and the F0 has already cancelled the running status (MIDI 1.0). For a SysEx received over USB (cable [address] = 2) it hits the unrelated DIN stream: a device on MIDI IN that uses running status (notes as data bytes only) loses every following message until it sends a new status byte (stuck notes possible: a note-off sent as note-on velocity 0 is lost too). Patch n°6 already stopped [routine] from doing the same; these four direct writes were left. Fix: the four writes move into two helpers in free flash (0x9d07b800-0x9d07b83f) that clear only when the SysEx cable is the DIN (the only cable whose SysEx goes through the DIN parser: [routine] [address], [routine] case 0xF0), then tail-jump to the leaf the site was calling ([routine] or [routine]). Cable = DIN: same writes as before. Real-time bytes F8-FF never touched the running status ([routine] [address]) and still do not.

edits.why: jal 0x9d07b800 ; case 5C: was "jal [address]" ([routine]); the running-status clear of the delay slot is done by the helper, only if the SysEx cable is the DIN
or s0,v0,zero ; case 60: was "sb zero,-0x7ea8(gp)"; the "move s0,v0" (result of [routine]) of the next delay slot moves here
jal 0x9d07b820 ; cases 61/62 last chunk: was "jal [address]" ([routine], a0 = 5 or 3 set by the branch delay slots)
nop ; cases 61/62 last chunk: was "sb zero,-0x7ea8(gp)"
jal 0x9d07b820 ; case 70 last chunk: was "jal [address]" ([routine]); delay slot "li a0,0x7" kept
nop ; case 70 last chunk: was "sb zero,-0x7ea8(gp)" (delay slot of "b [address]")
lui t0,0xa001 ; SysEx cable [address] (0 None, 1 DIN, 2 USB)
bne t0,t1,0x9d07b818 ; USB (or None): the DIN running status belongs to another stream, keep it
DIN: [address] = 0 as before (leaves the F0 header mode; the F0 already cancelled the running status)
j [address] ; [routine] (leaf, returns the command in v0 to the original call site)
lui t0,0xa001 ; same test; a0 (substate) is untouched
j [address] ; [routine](a0) (leaf), returns to the original call site
